# forumulate_domain (Resource)

A custom hostname for a space or a whole site. Creating one claims the name and returns the DNS records to publish (`dns_target`, `verification_record`: feed them to your DNS provider's resource). Nothing is served at the name until it is verified and activated: set `activate = true` once the records exist and the next apply verifies and switches traffic over (apply again after DNS propagates if the first attempt warns).

Exactly one of `space_id` or `site_id` is required. `redirect_to` and `ip_allow_list` exist on a space's domain only.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "forumulate_domain" "docs" {
  space_id          = forumulate_space.docs.id
  hostname          = "docs.example.com"
  also_redirect_www = false

  # Set once the DNS records below exist; the apply that follows verifies the
  # name and switches traffic over (apply again after DNS propagates).
  activate = true
}

# Publish the records with your DNS provider.
output "docs_dns_target" {
  value = forumulate_domain.docs.dns_target
}

output "docs_dns_verification" {
  value = forumulate_domain.docs.verification_record
}

# A whole site behind one name.
resource "forumulate_domain" "site" {
  site_id  = forumulate_site.main.id
  hostname = "www.example.com"
}

# Retire an old name by redirecting it.
resource "forumulate_domain" "legacy" {
  space_id    = forumulate_space.docs.id
  hostname    = "old-docs.example.com"
  redirect_to = "https://docs.example.com"
}

# Docs only reachable from the office network.
resource "forumulate_domain" "internal" {
  space_id      = forumulate_space.internal.id
  hostname      = "internal.example.com"
  ip_allow_list = ["203.0.113.0/24"]
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `hostname` (String) The hostname, such as `docs.example.com` (no scheme or path). Changing it replaces the domain.

### Optional

- `activate` (Boolean) Verify the DNS records and switch traffic to the hostname. If the records are not there yet the apply warns and the next apply tries again.
- `also_redirect_www` (Boolean) Also answer `www.<hostname>` with a permanent redirect here. Use it when your own app does not already redirect www.
- `base_path` (String) Serve under this path of the hostname instead of its root, such as `/docs` (up to 120 characters). Changing it replaces the domain.
- `external_ref` (String) Your own reference, fixed at creation: a repeat create naming it answers the existing domain.
- `ip_allow_list` (Set of String) Only these networks (CIDR ranges or addresses, up to 200) may read the hostname. A space domain only.
- `metadata` (Map of String) Tags an orchestrator keeps on the domain. Replaced whole. The API does not return them on a read, so drift is not detected.
- `redirect_to` (String) Permanently redirect the whole hostname to this URL (for retiring a name). A space domain only.
- `site_id` (String) The site the hostname serves, every member space at one address. Changing it replaces the domain.
- `space_id` (String) The space the hostname serves (its id or slug). Exactly one of `space_id` and `site_id`. Changing it replaces the domain.

### Read-Only

- `active` (Boolean) Whether traffic is served at the hostname.
- `created_at` (String) When the domain was claimed.
- `dns_target` (Attributes) The record that points the hostname at Forumulate: `type` (`A` or `CNAME`), `name` and `value`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--dns_target))
- `id` (String) The domain's id (a UUID).
- `verification_record` (Attributes) The TXT record that proves you own the hostname: `name` and `value`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--verification_record))
- `verified` (Boolean) Whether the DNS records prove ownership.

<a id="nestedatt--dns_target"></a>
### Nested Schema for `dns_target`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) The record's host name.
- `type` (String) The DNS record type (`A`, `CNAME`).
- `value` (String) The record's value.


<a id="nestedatt--verification_record"></a>
### Nested Schema for `verification_record`

Read-Only:

- `name` (String) The record's host name.
- `value` (String) The record's value.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

```shell
terraform import forumulate_domain.docs space/docs/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
terraform import forumulate_domain.site site/main/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000
```
